job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his grandmother, Dadi, were preparing lunch in their kitchen. Rohan suggested they only eat dal and ghee, as he thought protein was the only thing that mattered for his growth. Dadi smiled and explained that a balanced plate needs variety. She showed him a bowl of brown rice and millet rotis, explaining that whole grains provide essential fibre that keeps our digestion smooth, unlike refined maida which loses its goodness during polishing. Rohan then pointed to a vitamin tablet he took earlier, claiming it replaced his need for a full meal since it provided energy. Dadi shook her head, clarifying that while vitamins and minerals are vital for health, they do not provide the energy calories that carbohydrates and fats do. She added that a growing boy needs a mix of nutrients, not just one type. She also reminded him that his younger sister, who plays sports, needs a different portion size than their grandfather, who is less active. Finally, Dadi served a large portion of green leafy vegetables alongside a small portion of potatoes, noting that while potatoes are energy-rich, they cannot replace the unique micronutrients found in dark green vegetables. Rohan realized that a healthy diet is a thoughtful balance of different food groups tailored to each person's specific needs.

items.evidence: She added that a growing boy needs a mix of nutrients, not just one type.
items.q: Rohan wants to eat only dal and ghee for growth. Why does Dadi disagree?
options: His body needs many kinds of nutrients together
Dal alone gives every nutrient his body needs
His body cannot get protein from dal at all
Ghee will make him fat, but rice will not
items.explain: Dadi says a growing boy needs a mix of nutrients, not just one type like protein.

wrong.why: thinks one healthy food is enough
thinks only oily food adds weight

items.evidence: She showed him a bowl of brown rice and millet rotis, explaining that whole grains provide essential fibre that keeps our digestion smooth, unlike refined maida which loses its goodness during polishing.
items.q: Why does Dadi choose brown rice and millet rotis instead of maida?
options: Their fibre helps the stomach digest food easily
Their polishing makes them finer and cleaner
Their energy matters, as fibre is useless
Their protein is the only thing growth needs
items.explain: Whole grains give fibre for smooth digestion; maida loses its goodness when polished.

wrong.why: thinks polished grains are cleaner and better
repeats Rohan's earlier wrong idea about protein

items.evidence: Dadi shook her head, clarifying that while vitamins and minerals are vital for health, they do not provide the energy calories that carbohydrates and fats do.
items.q: Rohan took a vitamin tablet in the morning. Can he skip lunch?
options: He still needs lunch, as vitamins give no energy
He can skip lunch, as the tablet gives energy
He still needs lunch, but only dal for protein
He can skip lunch, as minerals replace carbohydrates
items.explain: Vitamins and minerals keep us healthy but give no energy calories; carbohydrates and fats do.

wrong.why: thinks protein is the only thing that matters
mixes up minerals with energy foods

items.evidence: She also reminded him that his younger sister, who plays sports, needs a different portion size than their grandfather, who is less active.
items.q: Should Rohan's sister, who plays sports, eat the same portion as Grandfather?
options: No, she uses more energy, so needs more
Yes, a balanced plate is same for everyone
No, Grandfather is older, so needs more
Yes, if both plates have enough protein
items.explain: The active sister needs a different portion from the less active grandfather; needs differ by person.

wrong.why: thinks everyone needs the same diet
thinks protein alone makes a plate balanced

items.evidence: Finally, Dadi served a large portion of green leafy vegetables alongside a small portion of potatoes, noting that while potatoes are energy-rich, they cannot replace the unique micronutrients found in dark green vegetables.
items.q: What would Rohan miss if he ate only potatoes instead of leafy greens?
options: Vitamins and minerals that dark greens give
No nutrients, as potato is a vegetable too
Energy, as potatoes give less than greens
No nutrients, if he eats enough potatoes
items.explain: Potatoes give energy but cannot replace the special micronutrients found in dark green vegetables.

wrong.why: thinks potato counts like leafy greens
thinks plenty of one food is enough
